title: Project Structure and Source Sets
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of project structure and source sets using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates project structure and source sets.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Project Structure and Source Sets** as part of **Packages, Modules, Dependencies, and Build Tools**. A set models unique elements, so use it when membership and uniqueness matter more than preserving duplicate entries. Use the subtopics—Main and Test Sources, Resources and Generated Outputs, Organizing Packages and Files—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A set models unique elements, so use it when membership and uniqueness matter more than preserving duplicate entries.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with main and test sources. Then compare it with resources and generated outputs. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Main and Test Sources
items.text: Main and Test Sources helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: Resources and Generated Outputs
items.text: Resources and Generated Outputs is one part of project structure and source sets. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Organizing Packages and Files
items.text: Organizing Packages and Files is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A read-only collection reference proves that no code can mutate the underlying data.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
